subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should the bundled Slack plugin own `assistant.search.context`, and what token lifetime, scope, and read-target policy should govern Slack RTS searches?
rationale: This crosses event-scoped Slack credentials, workspace search visibility, and OpenClaw's existing Slack read authorization boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent security contract.

options.title: Add narrow RTS support
options.body: Implement Slack-owned RTS search with ephemeral action-token handling, read-target policy, redaction, docs, focused tests, and live Slack workspace proof.

options.title: Defer outside bundled Slack
options.body: Keep core Slack unchanged and require a ClawHub/plugin path until maintainers are ready to own the RTS security boundary.

options.title: Reject workspace search for now
options.body: Keep Slack limited to conversation and thread reads and close future search attempts unless a maintainer sponsors the privacy model.

recommendation.title: Add narrow RTS support
recommendation.body: Implement Slack-owned RTS search with ephemeral action-token handling, read-target policy, redaction, docs, focused tests, and live Slack workspace proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent Slack assistant/action-surface history and closed the broad action-parity PR by routing Slack search back to this issue.
